steps.name: QC counts/metadata reconciliation and full-vs-reduced DESeq2 LRT
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes show a condition:time interaction — i.e., a temporal trajectory across t0..t3 that differs between the two conditions, beyond any trend shared by both conditions — using a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test comparing ~condition+time+condition:time against ~condition+time?
acceptance_criteria: Script first reconciles the 25 count columns against the 24-row metadata (report and resolve any mismatch such as a duplicated/extra sample column or a gene-symbol-as-column artifact before modeling; do not silently drop or duplicate a sample)
Raw integer counts loaded with gene symbols as rownames and a matching sample-ordered metadata data frame (condition, time as factor with levels t0,t1,t2,t3, time_hours retained for reference)
DESeqDataSet built with design ~condition + time + condition:time; DESeq() run with test='LRT' and reduced=~condition + time
Independent filtering and outlier handling left at DESeq2 defaults; results() extracted with alpha=0.05 and genes ranked by LRT p-value
Output table has one row per gene with LRT statistic, raw p-value, BH-adjusted p-value (interaction FDR), plus baseMean and log2FoldChange columns from the model matrix for interpretability

A separate results() call for the 'time' main-effect LRT (~condition+time vs ~condition) is also produced and reported alongside, explicitly to distinguish shared time-trend genes from interaction genes
Diagnostic PCA plot and dispersion plot saved to confirm design is well-behaved before interaction genes are trusted
Gene counts of interaction-significant (FDR<0.05) vs main-effect-only vs neither are reported explicitly

steps.name: Trajectory shapes of interaction-significant genes by condition
steps.question: Among genes with a significant condition:time interaction (T1S1), what distinct temporal trajectory shapes (per condition, across t0..t3) characterize the treatment-specific divergence, and do the two conditions diverge early (t0->t1) or only late (t2->t3)?
acceptance_criteria: Uses only genes flagged FDR<0.05 in the condition:time interaction LRT from T1S1 (not the main-effect-only set)
Variance-stabilized (vst or rlog) expression extracted for these genes, averaged per condition x time_point across the 3 replicates

Z-scored per-gene trajectories clustered separately by condition (hierarchical clustering, e.g. via amap/fastcluster/mclust as available) into a small number of shape clusters (e.g. up-in-treatment-only, down-in-treatment-only, transient, divergent-at-late-timepoint)
Heatmap of scaled trajectories (genes x condition:time) ordered by cluster and by time, produced with pheatmap or ComplexHeatmap
Report which time point first shows condition divergence for each cluster, based on the per-timepoint difference between condition trajectories
Cluster assignment table (gene, cluster label, trajectory shape) written out for downstream enrichment

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of condition-specific temporal genes
steps.question: Which biological pathways (WikiPathways, Reactome, MSigDB Hallmark) are over-represented among the genes showing a condition:time interaction, and do different trajectory-shape clusters (T1S2) map to distinct pathway themes?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the interaction-significant gene list (FDR<0.05) from T1S1 as the primary test set, with the full set of 12000 tested genes as background/universe

Runs over-representation (or fgsea rank-based, ranked by LRT statistic/log2FC) enrichment against the human WikiPathways GMT, the Reactome human-filtered GMT, and the MSigDB human Hallmark GMT located under the environment's reference store; if any of these is unavailable at run time, report which one and proceed with the remainder rather than failing the whole step
Reactome GMT is filtered to Homo sapiens pathway IDs using the accompanying Reactome pathway index before testing (the raw GMT spans all species)
Enrichment repeated separately for each trajectory-shape cluster from T1S2 (if cluster sizes permit, e.g. >=10 genes) to show which pathway themes belong to which divergence pattern
Output includes a results table per gene set collection with term name, gene ratio, adjusted p-value (BH), and the overlapping gene symbols
Multiple-testing correction applied within each gene-set collection separately, and this choice stated in the output

steps.name: PPI network context for interaction genes (exploratory)
steps.question: Do the genes with a significant condition:time interaction (T1S1) cluster within known STRING protein-protein interaction modules more than expected by chance, suggesting coordinated treatment-specific regulatory or signaling modules?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the human STRING v12.0 protein links and protein info files from the reference store; info file joined to links file to map STRING internal IDs to gene symbols before any analysis
High-confidence edges only (combined_score >= 700) used to build an undirected graph; edge duplication (each STRING edge appears twice) explicitly collapsed before reporting an edge count

Subgraph induced on the interaction-significant gene set from T1S1 (mapped to STRING IDs via the info file); network density and connected-component structure reported for this subgraph versus a size-matched random gene set (permutation or degree-preserving null) to assess whether observed connectivity exceeds chance
Report explicitly that this is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating network view — not a causal or confirmed-interaction claim, given STRING's known false-positive rate at the edge level
Any interaction genes absent from the STRING mapping are reported as unmapped rather than silently dropped without a count

plan.title: Condition x Time interaction DE in 2x4 time course
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2 condition x 4 time point (t0-t3) bulk RNA-seq time course, 3 replicates per cell (24 samples per the metadata, though the counts file carries 25 columns for 12000 genes — this column-count mismatch must be checked and reconciled against the metadata's sample IDs before any modeling). The research question asks for genes whose response over time differs BY CONDITION, beyond a trend shared by both conditions — this is precisely the condition:time interaction term in a full factorial design, and the standard, defensible way to isolate it is a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test (LRT) comparing a full model (~condition + time + condition:time) against a reduced model that drops the interaction (~condition + time). Genes significant in this LRT show a treatment-specific temporal pattern; genes significant only in a time main effect are shared drift and must be reported separately, not conflated. Time is treated as a categorical factor (t0..t3) rather than continuous/spline, since only 4 discrete time points exist and a categorical LRT test is the direct, standard DESeq2 approach for exactly this design (no maSigPro/ImpulseDE2/spline packages are available in this environment). After identifying interaction-significant genes, per-gene temporal trajectories are clustered separately within each condition to characterize the shape of the treatment-specific divergence, and the resulting gene set is tested for pathway enrichment against WikiPathways, Reactome, and MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (all present as human GMTs), giving biological interpretation to the interaction hits. A PPI-network view (STRING human v12.0) is added as a secondary, exploratory step to see whether interaction genes cluster within known protein interaction modules — useful context, not a load-bearing conclusion given the STRING network's high false-discovery character.
